ag_guide.text: That is Gelert's Grave. Don't tell the dog this, but the story is a lot older than the stone.
An innkeeper is supposed to have set the stone up to bring in visitors. Two hundred years on, it still works. Good marketing never goes out of style.

ag_volunteer.text: I give up my Saturdays to this railway. It is the best bad decision I ever made.
The line goes through the gorge and over the bridge, and the engine does the bit nobody can do on foot: it goes up without complaining.

ag_cafe.text: Bore da. Tea? Everyone says it is the water. I think it is the fact that I don't let anybody leave until they have had a cup.
The bara brith is my nain's recipe. I'm not allowed to say how much butter.

ag_gorge_walker.text: Keep to the path by the river. The rock is slippery when it is dry and unbelievable when it is wet.
The Aberglaslyn is the bit of Eryri people drive through and then say they will come back to. They do.

gate_aberglaslyn.text: The road to the Cambrian Coast is closed. Heritage Assessment. Director Pryce has not come back with the results.
He has been up the mountain for a good while now. I am sure it is all going very well.
